item.title: CXMT’s Rise to China’s Most Valuable Firm Heralds New Tech Era
item.description: CXMT Corp.’s ascent to the pinnacle of Chinese markets heralds a potentially consequential shift away from private-sector giants toward a new generation of hardware companies more closely aligned with Beijing’s strategic ambitions.

item.title: Alibaba to Sell Gaming Arm for $1.5 Billion in Boost to AI Pivot
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. is selling its gaming arm in a deal worth at least $1.5 billion that will boost the Chinese e-commerce leader’s pivot to AI.

item.title: Alphabet Hires Banks for Inaugural Aussie Dollar Bond Sale
item.description: Alphabet Inc. hired banks for what would be a debut offering of Australian dollar bonds, as US tech firms flood credit markets with debt to fund investments in AI.

item.title: Thai Baht Rally May Fade on Dovish Central Bank, Analysts Say
item.description: A nascent rally in the Thai baht may be short-lived as the central bank is likely to maintain a dovish policy stance to support an economy hit by elevated oil prices, according to analysts.

item.title: Japanese Idol App Firm Collapses Amid Wave of Bankruptcies
item.description: A Japanese company known for a game app based around virtual teen idols filed for bankruptcy, the latest in a wave of corporate failures that climbed to the most in 12 years as inflation and worker shortages hit weaker firms.

item.title: Japan’s Slower Growth Complicates BOJ’s Messaging on Rate Hike
item.description: Japan’s economic growth unexpectedly slowed in the three months through June, a result that may complicate the Bank of Japan’s policy communications as it weighs the timing of its next rate increase.

item.title: Gold Steady Near $4,400 as Traders Weigh US Data and Rate Path
item.description: Gold was steady as traders weighed the competing impacts of cooling US economic data and energy-led inflation pressure on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

item.title: WuXi AppTec’s 100% Stock Rally Defies Geopolitical Headwinds
item.description: The Pentagon’s designation of WuXi AppTec Co. as a Chinese military company may have prompted some US clients to pull back, but investors are still piling into the stock betting the firm will remain central to the global supply of obesity, cancer and other drugs.

item.title: A2 Milk Sees Slow Recovery From China Formula Supply Problem
item.description: New Zealand infant formula supplier a2 Milk expects only a gradual recovery from supply chain disruptions that impacted its China sales earlier this year, signaling the earnings margins will be soft in the six months through December.

item.title: Oil Edges Higher as Middle East Tensions Linger: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil opened slightly higher as traders weighed renewed Israeli attacks on Lebanon and the prospect of fresh US sanctions on Iran ahead of the formal end of the ceasefire due Monday.

item.title: National Australia Bank Profit Edges Up on Business Bank Growth
item.description: National Australia Bank Ltd.’s profit climbed in the third quarter as lending to businesses across the country expanded.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for June 17
item.description: Oil steadied as fresh fighting in Lebanon and attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz muddied the outlook for a deal to end the US-Iran war.

item.title: Trump Says Asked Pentagon to Cut Military Drills With S. Korea
item.description: “I have instructed Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to substantially reduce the Joint Military Exercises,” with South Korea, President Donald Trump says in a post on Truth Social.

item.title: BHP Heads Into Earnings With Least Amount of ‘Buy’ Ratings Ever
item.description: Analysts are less bullish on BHP Group Ltd. ahead of Tuesday’s full-year results, with buy recommendations for its Sydney-listed stock falling to a record low.

item.title: Skyrocketing Beef Prices Finally Have Americans Reaching Their Spending Limit
item.description: Aaron Kaufman used to meet his lofty daily protein goals — a gram for each pound he weighs — with ground beef.

item.title: Alex Cooper Leaves Long-Time Agent, Seeking New Help to Build Media Empire
item.description: Alex Cooper is leaving her long-time talent agent for CAA after raising money to expand her business

item.title: Stripe Clinches Over $7 Billion Deal to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter
item.description: Stripe Inc. has finalized an agreement to acquire OpenRouter Inc., a startup that helps companies switch between artificial intelligence models, for more than $7 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US 20-Year Bond Sale to Test Demand as Yield Curve Steepens
item.description: The sale of 20-year government bonds this week will test investor appetite for long-term debt following a few record-breaking auctions.

item.title: Stock-Market Calm Masks Fast Shifting Investor Sentiment
item.description: While the recent equity-market turbulence is subsiding, options positioning shows how quickly investor sentiment can switch between the extremes of fear and greed.

item.title: Second Ceuta Incursion Attempt Fails as Morocco, Spain Boost Security
item.description: Grassroots calls for a second incursion into Ceuta from Morocco fell flat over the weekend, with security tight and authorities turning back the relative handful who tried to make the move.

item.title: What’s Happening in EM: Traders Get Pickier on Linkers (Podcast)
item.description: Bogota-based EM reporter Nicolle Yapur joins Leda Alvim to discuss why investors are looking beyond Brazil and Mexico for opportunities in inflation-linked bonds in the emerging world.

item.title: At AI-Fueled Market Party, Wall Street Eyes the Rates Punch Bowl
item.description: Enthusiasm for Big Tech and its huge investments in artificial intelligence is powering the stock market to record highs again. With a resilient economy and scorching demand, there’s seemingly only one obstacle that can derail this ride: higher interest rates.

item.title: Traders Get Pickier After Big Run in $886 Billion EM Debt Market
item.description: Persistent inflation worries and currency swings are pushing emerging-market investors to adjust bets in an $886 billion asset class that’s been delivering outsize returns for more than a year.

item.title: Bonds Face a Bigger Threat Than the Fed as Global Rates Climb
item.description: As investors debate whether and when the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates, market expectations for further tightening are building around the world — and spelling trouble for bonds.

item.title: Israel Economy Rebounds After Contraction Sparked By Iran War
item.description: Israel’s economy rebounded in the second quarter, recovering from a contraction sparked by the military campaign against Iran.

item.title: Malaysia’s DAP Hands Anwar Reprieve With Vote to Stay in Cabinet
item.description: Malaysia’s Democratic Action Party voted on Sunday to remain in Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s cabinet, giving him a reprieve after a string of electoral setbacks and turmoil within his own party.

item.title: India Readies Big LPG Output Boost as Hormuz Uncertainty Lingers
item.description: India has directed its state companies and private refiners to prepare for a sharp increase in cooking gas production, seeking to bolster domestic supplies as the Iran war prolongs uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz, the key waterway for about 90% of the country’s liquefied petroleum gas imports.

item.title: Hong Kong’s First-Half Air Passenger Traffic Up 11.7%, Chan Says
item.description: Hong Kong’s airport passenger traffic jumped 11.7% on year in the first half, as the Asian financial hub hosted a variety of events and attracted more visitors, according to the city’s Financial Secretary Paul Chan.

item.title: Landing Your First Job Is Getting More Expensive in the UK
item.description: AI has raised the stakes of taking your first step up the career ladder - and made it tougher and costlier than ever.

item.title: China Plans to Speed Up New Energy Recycling, Waste Rules: CCTV
item.description: China is accelerating the establishment of rules governing the recycling and reuse of wind and solar equipment and aims to set up a closed-loop system for waste from the industry before 2030, China Central Television reported on Sunday.
